title: What can you say about resistant maltodextrin (soluble corn fiber) in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library gives no supported wording for resistant maltodextrin (soluble corn fiber), because no listed source supports one at a dose. Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Relieves constipation, without 'occasional'".

wordings_to_avoid.why: FDA's 2000 rule (page 1015) accepts only the 'occasional constipation' form.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Lowers blood sugar in diabetes, or helps manage diabetes

evidence_gap: No listed source gives a use with a dose for resistant maltodextrin: no Health Canada monograph for it is in the monograph list, Regulation (EU) No 432/2012 has no claim for it, there is no ODS fact sheet among those read, and FDA lists no health claim. FDA's dietary fiber question-and-answer page returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-14, so FDA's view of it as dietary fiber was not read.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
